None of the three solutions is correct. A direct count gives 7, which does not match any of their answers.

**Counting method.** The map (a,b) ↦ (k,ℓ) = (ap+3b, 2a+bq) is linear with determinant D = pq − 6.

- If D = 0, any integer value of k fixes a whole segment of (a,b), so there are infinitely many pairs. These cases are excluded.
- Otherwise the open unit square maps to the open parallelogram with vertices (0,0), (p,2), (3,q), (p+3,q+2). Its area is |D|, and every lattice point inside has k, ℓ > 0, so each one gives a valid (a,b). The number of valid pairs is therefore the number of interior lattice points.
- The boundary has 2(gcd(p,2) + gcd(3,q)) lattice points. By Pick's theorem, the interior count is |D| − gcd(p,2) − gcd(q,3) + 1.

Setting this equal to 14 gives |pq − 6| = 13 + gcd(p,2) + gcd(q,3).

| p | q | \|pq−6\| | pq | Valid (p,q) | Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| odd | 3∤q | 15 | 21 | (3,7), (21,1) | 2 |
| odd | 3∣q | 17 | 23 | none | 0 |
| even | 3∤q | 16 | 22 | (2,11), (22,1) | 2 |
| even | 3∣q | 18 | 24 | (2,12), (4,6), (8,3) | 3 |

The case pq − 6 < 0 gives no solutions. The total is 2 + 0 + 2 + 3 = 7.

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 claims (9,2) works, but there D = 12 and the interior count is 12 − 1 − 1 + 1 = 11, not 14.
- Solution 2 only considers pq < 6, which is wrong.
- Solution 3's claim that pq = 20 works is unjustified.

Since all three are wrong, I am picking Solution 1 arbitrarily.

CHOICE: 1
